etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from French intransigeant, from Spanish intransigente, from Latin in- (“un-, not”) + trānsigēns, present participle of trānsigō (“to come to an understanding”), from trāns (“across”) +‎ agō (“to do”).
senses: Unwilling to compromise or moderate a position; unreasonable; stubborn.
